# Research Context

## Clinical Topics

- TOPIC-PRP (Platelet-Rich Plasma)

## Research Question

In patients with knee osteoarthritis, do intra-articular Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP)
injections improve clinical outcomes compared with intra-articular Hyaluronic Acid (HA)?

## Clinical Problem

PRP and HA are both widely used intra-articular injections for knee osteoarthritis, but
their comparative effectiveness is debated. This review pools Level 1 RCTs to compare
them.

---

# Study Design

## Population

Pooled population of **811 patients** across **18 randomized controlled trials** of
patients with knee osteoarthritis.

## Inclusion Criteria

Level 1 randomized controlled trials comparing intra-articular PRP with intra-articular
HA in knee osteoarthritis. (Exact criteria to be confirmed against the full text.)

## Exclusion Criteria

Not extracted from the available abstract/summary — to confirm against the full text.

## Intervention

Intra-articular Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) injection.

## Comparator

Intra-articular Hyaluronic Acid (HA) injection.

## Outcomes

Primary outcomes: patient-reported clinical scores — WOMAC (total and physical
function), VAS (pain), IKDC.

Secondary outcomes: comparison of leukocyte-rich (LR-PRP) versus leukocyte-poor
(LP-PRP) formulations.

## Follow-up

Outcomes reported at 3, 6 and 12 months.

---

# Results

## Primary Findings

Intra-articular PRP was associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with HA in
the treatment of knee osteoarthritis.

## Secondary Findings

PRP was superior to HA in WOMAC total, WOMAC physical function and VAS scores at 3, 6
and 12 months. In the LR-PRP versus LP-PRP comparison, there was no significant
difference in WOMAC or VAS scores, while LP-PRP may be superior to LR-PRP in IKDC
scores.

## Statistical Significance

Between-group differences favouring PRP were reported as statistically significant for
the pooled patient-reported outcomes. (Exact effect sizes and confidence intervals to
be confirmed against the full text.)

## Clinical Significance

The direction of benefit favours PRP over HA for pain and function in knee OA; whether
the magnitude exceeds the minimal clinically important difference should be confirmed
against the full text.

# Evidence Quality

## Study Quality

★★★★★  (systematic review / meta-analysis of Level 1 RCTs)

## Risk of Bias

- Low
- Moderate
- High

Not determined from the available abstract/summary — to assess against the full text
(pooled RCTs vary in blinding, PRP preparation and HA product).

## Main Limitations

- Heterogeneity of PRP preparation protocols across the included trials.
- Heterogeneity of HA products and injection regimens.
- Most trials enrol general knee OA populations, not specifically young or
  post-traumatic patients.

## External Validity

Applies to knee osteoarthritis broadly. Generalisability to young, active,
post-traumatic knee OA is uncertain because the pooled trials are not specific to that
subgroup.

---

# Contribution to Current Knowledge

## Does this paper reinforce existing evidence?

Yes / Partially / No — **Yes.** It reinforces, at Level 1, that PRP tends to outperform
HA on patient-reported outcomes in knee OA.

## Does this paper contradict existing evidence?

Explain. — It does not clearly contradict prior evidence; it strengthens the PRP-over-HA
signal. It nuances the leukocyte-concentration debate (no WOMAC/VAS difference; possible
IKDC edge for LP-PRP).

## Does this paper introduce new knowledge?

Explain. — It consolidates 18 RCTs into a single Level 1 estimate and adds a
formulation subgroup comparison (LR-PRP vs LP-PRP).

---

# Relevance

## Applicable Patient Profiles

Adults with knee osteoarthritis considering an intra-articular injection (PRP vs HA).

## Non-applicable Profiles

Patients whose situation is not represented by the pooled trials — e.g. specifically
young, active, post-traumatic knee OA — should not over-extrapolate the pooled estimate.

---

# Open Questions

- What are the exact effect sizes and confidence intervals for each outcome and
  timepoint?
- How durable is the benefit beyond 12 months?
- Does the benefit hold specifically for young, active, post-traumatic knee OA?
- Which PRP preparation protocol is optimal?
